title: Banh Mi
subtitle: Vietnamese baguette sandwich with pickled vegetables and pork
excerpt: Banh mi is Vietnam's great sandwich. A light, crisp baguette holds a filling of pork, pickled daikon and carrot, coriander, chilli, and mayonnaise. The combination of French bread and Vietnamese flavours reflects the country's colonial history. It is one of the most satisfying handheld meals anywhere.
sourceNotes: Banh mi literally means wheat bread -- a reference to the French baguette introduced during colonial rule. After independence, Vietnamese bakers created a lighter, airier version. The sandwich as we know it evolved in Saigon in the 1950s, combining French bread and pate with Vietnamese aromatics. It is now eaten worldwide.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pickled carrot can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: The quick-pickled carrot is the backbone of a good banh mi. Make it first and let it sit while you cook the pork. The vinegar, sugar, and salt brine takes 3 minutes to put together. Twenty minutes is enough to soften and sharpen the carrot -- longer is better if you have time.

items.prepNote: use pork belly or Vietnamese pork roll if available -- or pork mince formed into small patties
use 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp fish sauce combined
for the quick pickle -- mix with 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
serve in a baguette or crusty white roll -- split lengthways

content.text: Make the quick pickle: mix the vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved. Add the carrot matchsticks. Toss and leave for at least 20 minutes.
Season the pork mince with soy sauce and fish sauce. Shape into small patties or leave as mince. Cook in a hot frying pan with a little oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through.
Split the baguettes lengthways. Spread both halves with mayonnaise.
Add a layer of pork, then pickled carrot, spring onion, fresh coriander, and chilli.
Close the sandwich and serve immediately.

items.cause: Pickled vegetables too wet or added while still hot
items.fix: Drain the pickled vegetables well before adding. Let the pork cool for a minute before filling the sandwich. Assemble just before serving -- banh mi does not travel well once built.

content.text: Banh mi is sold from street carts across Vietnam, particularly in Ho Chi Minh City. The Vietnamese baguette is lighter and crispier than a French baguette -- the crust shatters. The combination of pickled carrot, pate or pork, mayonnaise, and coriander is the classic template. Every vendor has their own version.
